title: Copyable content with a high-emotional-reward element gets reduced to that element by users seeking the strongest hit, despite the creator's intent
body:
- When content is freely copyable and contains elements that trigger strong emotional responses, a subset of users seeking maximum emotional impact will extract only those elements
- Extracting the high-reward element removes the surrounding nuance and context, which is what produces the strongest emotional hit per exposure
- The creator cannot prevent this once the content is released, because copyability gives anyone the ability to isolate and redistribute any element
- The pattern is predictable: content with a high-reward element tends to be remembered and propagated only in that mode
conversion: A creator's full work becomes reduced to its high-emotional-reward element when users seeking the strongest emotional hit can extract it from its context
